subject: Acme MAP: Technical evaluation plan (benchmarks, targets, shortlist)
messages:
From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro / MAP kickoff - follow-up and technical evaluation scope

Hi Marissa / Camila —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from Acme's side and shifts we discussed:

- Goal: Proof-of-concept to replace our legacy NLU pipeline for customer support triage (initial scope: English only).
- Success criteria (business): 10% reduction in misrouted tickets, maintain/beat current SLA on intent classification.
- Technical ask: we need a short, runnable technical evaluation plan (MAP milestone) that lists benchmark success criteria, latency and cost targets, and a model shortlist that we can test in our environment.

Next steps we agreed on:
1) Redwood to share MAP draft with milestones and responsibilities (incl. technical eval plan) by next week.
2) Acme to share a small sample dataset (~5k anonymized tickets) and current baseline metrics.
3) Align on target close date for POC (we suggested mid-May).

Attaching the MAP template Acme uses internally — please populate the technical eval milestone section.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Nguyen
Head of AI Products | Acme Corp.
[Attachment: acme-map-v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro / MAP kickoff - follow-up and technical evaluation scope

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the clear recap. Attached is a draft MAP with the technical evaluation milestone filled out. High level summary below; full details are in the attached PDF (also pasted key points).

MAP milestone: Technical evaluation plan (owner: Redwood + Acme)
- Objective: Validate model accuracy, latency, and cost on a representative subset of Acme tickets.
- Timeline: 2 weeks of bench testing + 1 week integration tests. Target close for the POC milestone: 2027-05-15.
- Success criteria (benchmarks):
  • Intent classification F1 >= 0.88 (macro) OR >= 8% improvement vs Acme baseline (whichever is easier to measure).
  • Entity extraction average F1 >= 0.85 for key entities.
  • Latency: p95 end-to-end inference latency <= 150 ms for a 256-token request (measured from request arrival to token stream start in Redwood sandbox).
  • Cost target: inference cost <= $0.30 per 1k input tokens at projected QPS after batching (approximate target; final numbers depend on model/config).
- Model shortlist (to run on Redwood hosted sandbox + Dedicated test nodes):
  1) meta-llama-2-13b (float16 & 4-bit quantized)
  2) mistral-large (float16 & 4-bit quantized)
  3) redwood/open-7b (optimized kernels + int8 quantized)
  4) experimental: mosaic-ml/decoder-variant-13b (if allowed by licensing)
- Benchmark plan:
  • Redwood will run 3 repeatable benchmark runs per model (cold KV cache + warm cache) using Acme's sample dataset and standardized prompts.
  • Measure: accuracy metrics (F1/precision/recall), latency p50/p95, memory utilization, and per-1k-token cost estimate.
  • Failure conditions: any model failing to meet latency p95 or accuracy floor will be documented and excluded from the shortlist.
- Responsibilities:
  • Acme: provide anonymized sample dataset (5k) + baseline metrics and define final acceptance criteria. Provide access window for integration tests.
  • Redwood: prepare sandbox access, run benchmarks, deliver benchmark report (PDF) and recommended config (batching, quantization, routing policy).
  • Timeline owner: Marissa Cole (Redwood) — coordinate test windows, resource allocation, and final report.
- Dependencies / blockers:
  • Dataset delivery (Acme) — expected by 2027-04-15 (if delayed, timeline shifts).
  • Procurement for Dedicated nodes (if Acme needs on-prem/Dedicated for POC).

Attachments: redwood-map-draft-ACME-technical-eval.pdf, redwood-benchmark-instructions.md

Let us know if you want different latency/cost targets or to add any additional models. Happy to jump on a quick 30-min sync.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
Schedule: https://calendly.com/marissa-redwood/30
[Attachment: redwood-map-draft-ACME-technical-eval.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro / MAP kickoff - follow-up and technical evaluation scope

Hi all — quick clarification on Marissa's latency spec: when we say p95 <= 150 ms, we mean p95 for end-to-end inference within Redwood sandbox with standard batching (target QPS ~10). Measurement notes we will include:

- Measurement window: 5k requests spread over a 10-minute run; report both cold-start (first run) and steady-state (after warm-up).
- Request shape: 256 input tokens avg, up to 512 tokens max.
- Include both streaming-start latency (time-to-first-token) and full-response latency in appendix.

If Acme prefers a different QPS or token shape, we can adjust.

Camila Reyes
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
